speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy; have you noticed any vomiting, and if so, does it ever look like it contains bile or food coming back up?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Patient
text: The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Intussusception and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is reassuring, but we need to confirm the diagnosis to plan treatment. Have the baby had any episodes of "currant jelly" stools—stools that are bloody or look like red jelly?

REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.
REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The ultrasound showing dilated bowel segments, the absence of rectal gas, and the clinical history of feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, and suspected "currant jelly" stools confirm an intestinal obstruction consistent with intussusception. Immediate surgical reduction or air enema is required.
